title: Functorial enlargement of a bounded finitely presented complex
statement: For a scheme morphism f:X -> S [def-pc-scheme] and composable morphisms T'' -> T' -> T over S [def-pc-base-change], any bounded integer-indexed complex H of finitely presented modules on X_T has a bounded finitely presented complex K on X_T', termwise isomorphic to the base change of H. Its further base change to X_T'' is termwise isomorphic to the direct base change of H, compatibly with all differentials. No flatness, inverse limit, or new descent assertion is involved.

proof.text: Apply moduleBaseChange to H degreewise. It is a left adjoint, so preserves zero morphisms and zero objects, giving a complex with the same bounded interval.
Apply tensor-pullback finite-presentation preservation to each term.

baseChangeMap_comp and nonempty_tensorPullbackComp give a natural functor isomorphism between direct and successive base change. Its components provide the limit comparison and its naturality proves differential compatibility.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_bounded_complex_baseChange_enlargement
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) {T T' T'' : Over S}
    (g : T' ⟶ T) (h : T'' ⟶ T')
    (H : CochainComplex (pullback f T.hom).Modules ℤ)
    (hH_bounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (H.X n))
    (hH_fp : ∀ n : ℤ, (H.X n).IsFinitePresentation) :
    ∃ K : CochainComplex (pullback f T'.hom).Modules ℤ,
      (∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (K.X n)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, (K.X n).IsFinitePresentation) ∧
      (Nonempty (∀ n : ℤ, K.X n ≅ (Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChange f g).obj (H.X n))) ∧
      ∃ e : ∀ n : ℤ,
        (Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChange f h).obj (K.X n) ≅
          (Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChange f (h ≫ g)).obj (H.X n),
        ∀ n m : ℤ,
          (Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChange f h).map (K.d n m) ≫ (e m).hom =
            (e n).hom ≫ (Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChange f (h ≫ g)).map (H.d n m)
